XPm_IsMemRegnAddressValid() for boot and runtime-eemi, check whether given subsystem is accessible during boot-time XPm_IsMemRegnAddressValid() for runtime-subsys, check whether given address range falls in mem-regn
For runtime, IsPLMem flag is used to also check PL Power Domain ( IsPLMem flag is don't care for boot & eemi )

For Non-PL Mem-Regns, reachability is decided by the parent controller device(s); delegate to the shared device-reachability core. EnableLog=1U preserves this validator's original per-device diagnostic logging.

briefdescription.para: Checks whether a given address range (addr + size) is fully reachable through RUNNING memory-controller devices (OCM/TCM/DDR).

parameterdescription.para: Start Address of the range
Size of the range
1U => emit the per-device diagnostic PmErr logs ("Node not running" and "Mismatch Memory type access!"); 0U => silent.

simplesect.para:
Status of the operation:
XPM_SUCCESS: entire range contained in RUNNING device(s)
XPM_PM_NO_ACCESS: range found but a part not RUNNING
XPM_ERR_MEM_ACCESS_TYPE: cross-type overlap
XPM_FAILURE: range not found / unresolved overlap

Shared reachability core used by XPm_IsMemAddressValid() and the memory-table State projection. The per-device diagnostic PmErr logs ("Node not running" and "Mismatch Memory type access!" - 4 in total) are gated by EnableLog: XPm_IsMemAddressValid() passes 1U to preserve its original logging, while the high-frequency State refresh passes 0U to stay silent (no log spam). Return codes are identical for both callers.
